Look up the digit a resistor band's color stands for, and list the colors in value order.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/resistor-color) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: resistor_color.nomi
//# The values of a resistor's color bands.

/// A band color, in value order: black is 0 and white is 9.
pub enum Color {
    Black
    Brown
    Red
    Orange
    Yellow
    Green
    Blue
    Violet
    Grey
    White
}

derive Variants for Color

/// The digit `color` stands for on a band.
pub fn color_code(color: Color) -> Int {
    case color {
        .Black -> 0
        .Brown -> 1
        .Red -> 2
        .Orange -> 3
        .Yellow -> 4
        .Green -> 5
        .Blue -> 6
        .Violet -> 7
        .Grey -> 8
        .White -> 9
    }
}

/// Every band color, in value order.
pub fn colors() -> List<Color> {
    Color.variants()
}

// FILE: resistor_color_test.nomi
import {
    resistor_color
    resistor_color.Color
}

test "Color codes" {
    cases = [
        #("Black", Color.Black, 0),
        #("White", .White, 9),
        #("Orange", .Orange, 3),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, color, expected), description {
        assert resistor_color.color_code(color) == expected
    }
}

test "Colors" {
    assert resistor_color.colors() == [
        Color.Black,
        .Brown,
        .Red,
        .Orange,
        .Yellow,
        .Green,
        .Blue,
        .Violet,
        .Grey,
        .White,
    ]
}
```

## How it's written

- The colors are an enum, `Color`, rather than the canonical strings; the tests write `Color.Black` where the data says `"black"`.
- `color_code` spells each value out in a `case` rather than taking the color's position in `Color.variants()`. The position would need a search that answers a `Maybe`, and the table is what the problem states.
- `colors` is `Color.variants()` from `derive Variants`, which lists the variants in declaration order, the value order.
- The expected list in the `Colors` test qualifies only its first element (`[Color.Black, .Brown, ...]`); the later bare variants take its enum.
